transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, what brings me in... well, honestly, it's work. I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore, even when it's really important. Like, I'm a computer support specialist, right? So I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and... you know, networks have gotten so complicated lately. Back when I started, we were dealing with basic token ring setups, but now everything is cloud-based and hybrid, and the documentation vendors provide is just garbage. I mean, absolute garbage. I had this one guy from Cisco try to explain their new licensing model to me last week, and I swear he didn't even understand it himself. He kept talking about... oh, right, sorry. The problem is, I'll be looking at the network issue, and ten minutes later I realize I've reread the same log entries three times and I still have no idea what they actually say. It's just... it's really getting bad.
Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?

Yeah, actually. My mom still jokes about it to this day. She says my grade school report cards always said the exact same thing—that I was bright, but I never stayed in my seat, and I was constantly blurting out answers. And the homework... man, I'd actually do the work and then just completely lose it before I could turn it in. 

Which is ironic because my mom, she kept all those old report cards in this big green accordion folder. You know those
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or euphoric and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I have days where I feel pretty good, but not like... euphoric. And sleep? Man, I wish I could get by on less sleep. I try to get my eight hours, but my dog—he's a golden retriever mix, adopted him about two years ago from this shelter out in the valley. Great dog, really smart, but he has this thing where he wakes up at exactly 4:15 AM every single morning. Doesn't matter if it's a weekday, weekend, raining, snowing... 4:15, he's up and whining at the door. I've tried taking him on longer walks at night to tire him out, and I even bought this special puzzle toy that dispenses treats, you know, to keep his brain busy. But nope. 4:15. So yeah, I'm usually pretty exhausted, definitely not energized.
How much alcohol do you usually drink in a typical week?

Alcohol? Um, I don't really drink. None, I guess. I mean, maybe a beer at a barbecue once or twice a year, but that's it. I just never really got the appeal, you know? Plus, with my stomach... I had this awful bout of acid reflux a few years back. Thought I was having a heart attack, honestly. I went to the ER and everything. The doctor there—he looked just like that guy from that medical show, what's his name... the one with the cane? Anyway, he told me to cut out spicy foods, coffee, and alcohol. And I love coffee, I really do. I have this French press that makes the most amazing dark roast, gets shipped to me from this little roaster in Seattle. My sister lives out there, actually. She's a graphic designer. But yeah, no alcohol for me.
Do these attention problems also cause trouble for you outside of work?

Yeah, definitely. It's... it's really messed things up for me lately. Ever since I lost the structure of my old job, my reputation has just taken a massive hit. I've been trying to do some freelance stuff, but I keep losing clients because I just can't seem to stay on top of things. And I even missed out on this senior service-manager role I was up for. People just don't trust me to follow through anymore, and it's putting a lot of stress on my wife and me because now we're worrying about money. 

Which is awful, because my wife, she's usually the one who handles the finances. She's got this whole system with color-coded spreadsheets. She actually learned how to do all that Excel programming—macros and pivot tables and whatever—from this online course she took during the pandemic. We were stuck in the house for months, and she just decided to learn spreadsheets. I tried to learn how to bake sourdough bread like everyone else was doing, but I kept forgetting to feed the starter. You have to feed it every day, like a pet, and it just got moldy and I had to throw the whole jar away. It was a nice jar, too, one of those thick glass ones with the wire clamp lid. We used to keep coffee beans in it. But yeah, the money stuff is really stressing us out right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Down or depressed? No, not really. I mean, I'm stressed about the money and the job stuff, obviously, but not depressed. I actually felt pretty good yesterday because I finally got around to cleaning out the garage. Well, part of the garage. I started with this old workbench that belonged to my grandfather. He was a carpenter, built these beautiful wooden boats up in Maine. Real craftsmanship, you know? Not like the cheap plywood stuff you buy at the big box stores today. I still have some of his old hand planes. They're heavy, solid iron, but they're covered in rust now. I watched this whole series of videos on YouTube about how to restore antique hand tools using electrolysis. It's fascinating, really, how you can just use a car battery charger and some washing soda to reverse the rust. I bought the washing soda—had to go to three different grocery stores to find it, actually. The first two only had baking soda, which isn't the same thing. But anyway, yeah, I'm not depressed, just... stressed, I guess.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?

Worrying? No, not really. I mean, I worry about the bills and stuff, like I said, but not just... out of nowhere. If there's no problem, I don't really sit around worrying about one. Actually, I usually try to keep busy. Like with the garage thing. Or... oh, last week I decided I was going to fix the leaky faucet in the downstairs bathroom. It’s been dripping for months. Drip, drip, drip. Drives my wife crazy. So I went to the hardware store—the big one out on Route 9, not the local one, because the local one never has the right size O-rings. And while I was there, I saw they had this massive sale on outdoor lighting. Solar-powered pathway lights. We don't even have a pathway in the backyard, just grass, but they looked so nice, like little copper lanterns. I ended up buying a dozen of them. Spent like two hours trying to figure out the best pattern to put them in the grass. I still haven't fixed the faucet, actually. I should probably do that. But no, I don't really worry about things unless there's a reason to.
